data.title: Tires Easy Ranks No. 8 on Los Angeles Times' 2026 Fastest-Growing Companies List
data.description:
EL SEGUNDO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Tires Easy, a national online tire retailer, has been named the No. 8 fastest-growing private company in Los Angeles County by Business by LA Times Studios. The list recognizes the 50 privately held companies headquartered in Los Angeles County with the highest percentage revenue growth, highlighting business performance in one of the nation's largest and most diverse regional economies.

The 2026 ranking reflects the strength of Los Angeles County's business community. The 35 largest companies on the list generated more than $2.9 billion in combined 2025 revenue, nearly double their 2023 total. Companies were ranked according to verified revenue growth over the two years.

For Tires Easy, the recognition reflects a different approach to building a national retail business. Rather than operating its own chain of tire stores, the company uses an e-commerce platform, nationwide warehouse inventory and relationships with local installation providers to serve customers across the United States.

"Los Angeles County is home to some of the country's most ambitious and successful businesses, so earning a place among its fastest-growing companies is particularly meaningful," said Adam Barker, CEO of Tires Easy. "We believe customers should be able to shop for tires the way they shop for almost anything else online, with competitive pricing, a wide selection and convenient local installation. Our growth shows that this approach is working."

The company's proprietary pricing and inventory platform draws real-time information from more than 1,900 warehouses, providing access to more than 47,000 tire products across 200 brands. Customers can compare products and prices online and arrange installation through a network of more than 1,600 local service providers.

Tires Easy's performance has also earned national recognition. The company ranked No. 114 on the Financial Times 2026 Americas' Fastest-Growing Companies list and No. 759 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies.

The company's profile and growth figures are available on the Business by LA Times Studios website.

###

About Tires Easy

Founded in 2004 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Tires Easy is a national online tire retailer offering a broad selection of passenger, light truck and specialty tires. The company has sold more than 8 million tires since its founding and provides customers with access to competitive pricing, nationwide inventory and convenient local installation options. For more information, visit www.tires-easy.com.

data.title: Nvidia's stock falls further. It has lost $669 billion in six trading days.
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

There are only 20 companies in the world with a market capitalization of $669 billion or higher

Shares of Nvidia fell again on Thursday.

Nvidia shares initially opened higher on Thursday, fueled in part by optimism surrounding Anthropic's IPO, but they ended the day by clinching a six-day wipeout streak.

The stock (NVDA) closed down 3.3% on Thursday. The company has lost $669 billion in market capitalization over the past six trading days. There are only 20 companies in the world with a market capitalization of $669 billion or higher, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Nvidia's stock is down 16% over this period.

"I don't think the losing streak is over yet," said Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at Zeus Quanto, a quant strategy research platform.

Rakhmatov told MarketWatch that a number of factors were working against the stock, one being that credit-rating agency Moody's changed its outlook for Nvidia to stable from positive on Wednesday. A "positive" outlook indicates a higher likelihood that a company's credit rating could be upgraded in the medium term.

"That is not a rating downgrade, and nobody doubts Nvidia can pay its debts. But it puts the leadership gap in writing," he said.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's longtime CEO last week after admitting to an affair with a woman associated with a Singapore-based company that has been a large customer of Nvidia's chips. Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The board appointed Nvidia's chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to the position of interim CEO.

Rakhmatov said the uncertainty over the CEO position at Nvidia and the company's relationship with China are weighing on the stock. "Until there is a new CEO and the board's investigation ends, investors will apply a discount," he added.

Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told MarketWatch that the market has seen some of the most "aggressive de-risking across growth and AI stocks in years," with Nvidia's stock falling nearly 30% despite the company delivering "exceptional" financial results for its last reported quarter as recently as Tuesday, while raising its outlook for the full year.

Boloor said he's telling investors to "separate what's happening with Nvidia's stock from what's happening with Nvidia's business."

There's little evidence that demand for computing power is slowing, he said, noting that rental prices for graphics processing units are rising, among other factors.

"I still believe Nvidia is one of the most important companies in the AI economy, but that doesn't automatically make it a safe haven while those questions remain unanswered," he said.

Michael Casper, senior market strategist at HB Wealth, noted that Nvidia's stock saw a series of highs from November 2024 through January 2025 that "top out pretty much right at $150." Market technicians often look for "prior highs," especially ones that were "tested," meaning the price approaches the high and then breaks down.

Casper told MarketWatch that traders "are likely lining up to buy" at $150. But if the price falls below that level, then there's "more downside to come as people holding at that level go underwater on their trade and attempt to cut losses."

Shares of Nvidia closed at $145.98 on Thursday.

See also: Who can replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO? These four names are buzzing in AI circles.

Sentara Capital founder Will Allen pointed out to MarketWatch that $148.80 was the "capitulation low" last Thursday morning when Huang announced his resignation. "That is an important level in the near term," he said.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Intuit to Sell Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Intuit agreed to sell its email automation platform Mailchimp for $3.68 billion.

The fintech, which offers tax and accounting services, said it would sell the platform to Bending Spoons for $3.31 billion of cash and $368 million of Bending Spoons stock.

Intuit also posted higher profit and revenue in the fiscal first quarter.

Profit rose to $695 million, or $2.59 a share, compared with $446 million, or $1.59 a share, a year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted per-share earnings were $2.91, ahead of the $2.46 anticipated by analysts, according to FactSet.

Revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $4.30 billion. Sales in Intuit's business-facing segment increased 15%, while its consumer-facing sales rose 7%.

Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million in the quarter. Intuit said selling the business will allow the company to sharpen its focus on helping clients win new customers and manage their pipeline.

The sale of the business is expected to close early in 2027. Intuit plans to use cash proceeds to buy back shares of its stock within fiscal 2027.

Intuit now expects full-year revenue to be $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, compared with its earlier range of $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. It expects earnings per share of $20.12 to $20.36.

data.title: Illuminations at Botanica
data.description:
Illuminations at Botanica

Illuminations at Botanica

PR Newswire

WICHITA, Kan., Nov. 19, 2026

-- New Experiences. A Family Tradition. Wichita's Premier Holiday Light Display. --

WICHITA, Kan., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The holiday season is about to shine brighter than ever as Illuminations returns to Botanica from November 23, 2026, through January 2, 2027 with entry times at 5:30 PM, 6:30 PM, 7:30 PM, and 8:30 PM. Wichita's premier holiday light display will once again transform the gardens into a breathtaking winter wonderland, featuring more than two million twinkling lights, dazzling displays, festive music, a new Winter Rose Meadow installation, and exciting curated experiences for guests of all ages.

"It's an honor to host one of Wichita's favorite holiday traditions at Botanica, where our staff and volunteers build Illuminations right here in the gardens," says Dr. Lynette Zimmerman, Botanica's Executive Director. "As our largest fundraiser, Illuminations helps us care for the gardens, offer educational programs, and reach more people in our community throughout the year. We can't wait to welcome everyone to Wichita's premier holiday light display."

New this year is the Winter Rose Meadow. It features towering illuminated roses and glowing vines in the Children's Garden, and is the perfect place to pause for a photo. Guests can also watch the 62-foot Grand Tree light up in time with holiday music, explore miniature displays, listen to carolers, and visit Santa in his workshop. Rides on the Khicha Family Carousel are $3, and throughout the night, guests can sip hot cocoa, share s'mores nachos, or warm up with a dish from The Pasta Kitchen. They can also try a Kansas favorite: a bowl of chili served with a cinnamon roll. Specialty cocktails and mocktails are available throughout the gardens as well.

Admission prices are $19 for non-member adults, $15 for members, $12 for kids ages 3-12, and free for children 2 and under. Make sure to purchase your tickets on Botanica's website in advance to ensure you can attend on a day that works best for you. Don't miss out on this unforgettable holiday tradition. See you under the lights!

Opened in May 1987, Botanica welcomes visitors year-round to more than 30 themed gardens across 20 acres. Through its gardens, educational programs, and community events, Botanica cultivates lifelong curiosity, connection, and care for the natural world.

data.title: eXoZymes Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Provides Business Update at 5PM ET Today
data.description:
LOS ANGELES, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Today, eXoZymes Inc. (NASDAQ:EXOZ) ("eXoZymes") - a pioneer of AI-enhanced enzymes that transform abundant feedstock into valuable nutraceuticals and novel medicines - will host an investor webinar at 5:00 PM Eastern Time to discuss results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provide an update on recent business developments.

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, states, "We're entering an exciting new phase for eXoZymes as we advance our lead product toward commercial manufacturing while expanding our pipeline of high-value molecules. Our progress with Curia and the advancement of additional product candidates demonstrate how we intend to turn our technology into a repeatable engine for commercial opportunities. We believe our ability to move rapidly from discovery toward scalable production is what sets our platform apart."

Third quarter highlights

  • Commercial manufacturing preparations underway with Curia: In September, eXoZymes selected Curia as its commercial-scale manufacturing partner for NCT, the rare natural molecule behind its lead supplement brand, Tyferyn. Technology transfer began in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the collaboration intended to support larger-scale manufacturing in 2027, representing an important step toward commercial readiness.
  • Tyferyn introduced as the brand for human use: eXoZymes introduced Tyferyn as the new brand name for its lead nutraceutical ingredient focused on human wellness applications. The rebranding establishes a distinctive, consumer-friendly identity as the Company advances preparations for commercialization.
  • Product pipeline expands: eXoZymes has advanced two additional supplement candidates through proof of concept, demonstrating the broader potential of its cell-free biomanufacturing platform. Product SAPPHIRE, targeting joint comfort, has begun scale-up activities, while Product AMETHYST, targeting mental stress, focus and energy, has also completed proof of concept. The programs support the Company's strategy of building a diversified portfolio of high-value products using its shared enzyme technology and development capabilities.
  • Operational and financial update: Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $3.05 million, compared with $2.52 million for the same period in 2025. Net loss was $2.24 million for the quarter and $7.49 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net loss for the quarter includes a $0.77 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities. The Company ended the quarter with $3.26 million in cash and cash equivalents, which the Company expects will support operations through the beginning of 2027.

Investors and interested parties can access the live webinar through eXoZymes' investor relations website at:
https://video.exozymes.com/exoz-investor-update-3q26-nov-19

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, will lead the call and be joined by select members of the management team to review recent developments and ongoing initiatives. A recording and transcript of the conference call will also be made publicly available following the event.

Founded in 2019, eXoZymes is pioneering a cell-free biomanufacturing platform that uses AI-enhanced enzymes - called exozymes - to make valuable natural products and new analogs outside living cells. The company's platform is designed to replace inefficient extraction and petrochemical processes with a scalable way to produce high-value molecules for nutraceutical and pharmaceutical markets.

eXoZymes is building a portfolio of biosolutions across NCT - now Tyferyn for human use - cannabinoid analogs, santalene, and other high-value natural product molecules, with potential commercialization paths that include partnerships, licensing and joint ventures. Learn more at exozymes.com

data.title: Why Micron, Broadcom and other AI stocks gave up their gains Thursday
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

The Anthropic IPO enthusiasm faded while China concerns intensified

Micron's stock closed down about 2% on Thursday.

For a period of time on Thursday, it looked like the excitement over Anthropic's initial public offering would give artificial-intelligence stocks a much-awaited boost. But the trading action turned decidedly more mixed.

Shares of companies like Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) that initially saw a broad-based AI rally on Thursday morning closed lower. Some of the AI stocks that closed in positive territory on Thursday, including Intel (INTC) and Coherent (COHR), had their own specific catalysts.

Part of the issue may be that Anthropic's IPO prompted investors to shift around their holdings, according to Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at quantitative-strategy research platform Zeus Quanto.

"Investors who wanted the purest AI exposure got it today, and some of them sold Nvidia and other chip names to fund the new position," he told MarketWatch.

Granted, the excitement around Anthropic itself has also waned. Shares (ANT) opened 34% higher midday Thursday, but they pared those gains to close up 17% from their IPO price of $83.

Jack Amy, a quantitative-trading analyst at European digital wealth platform Moneyfarm, noted that at first, the Anthropic IPO "gave broader U.S. equities a lift, helping to steady nerves after a choppy week for tech."

"However, those wider gains have since pared back as macro concerns, specifically around tightening financial conditions and what that means for the capital-intensive AI trade, continue to weigh on sentiment," he added in emailed comments.

There are also renewed jitters about export policies after a report from a short seller discussed whether Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) chips have made it into Chinese servers.

"The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships. AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," an AMD spokesperson told MarketWatch.

"The China issues are likely to permeate across the semi industry as export controls are tightened," said Michael Casper, senior market strategist at wealth-management firm HB Wealth.

Investors have generally been worried that the U.S. government would take a tougher tack on sales of advanced technology to China in light of recent turmoil involving Nvidia.

See also: Jensen Huang was a 'China salesman' for Nvidia. His exit is weighing on Chinese tech stocks.

Heading into Thursday's trading day, D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that Anthropic's IPO was "pivotal" for the AI investment cycle.

Luria said that a successful IPO could "extend the cycle by years," while an unsuccessful one could "stall investment" into the ecosystem.

See also: Can Anthropic's IPO do for the stock market what Nvidia's earnings couldn't?

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski doubted the IPO would "fully turn around what has been very bearish sentiment lately." One reason is that investors saw Anthropic's prospectus weeks ago and knew "relatively what to expect."

The AI stocks that managed to hold onto some gains on Thursday had some idiosyncratic drivers. Shares of Coherent closed up 1% after the optical company announced a new buyback program, while shares of Intel closed up 2% following reports of remarks from a conference indicating that the company locked in an outside customer for its 18A manufacturing technology.

CoreWeave's stock, meanwhile, gave up a double-digit percentage gain and closed down 6%, despite a co-founder's disclosure that he purchased $30 million of the company's bruised bonds with the intention to hold them until maturity in 2031.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Rising healthcare costs push Medicare Part B premiums higher
data.description:
By Jessica Hall

The premiums will increase by $6.50, to $209.40 a month

Higher Medicare Part B premiums will erode part of the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027.

Medicare Part B premiums, which cover doctor's appointments, outpatient hospital services, and certain home health services, will rise about 3.2% to $209.40 a month in 2027 amid a projected increase in healthcare spending, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services said on Tuesday.

The premium will rise by $6.50 a month from $202.90 in 2026, which marked the first time premiums topped $200 a month. The higher premium for 2027, which would total $2,512.80 a year, was roughly in line with expectations set by the Social Security and Medicare Board of Trustees in June.

The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries will be $292 in 2027, an increase of $9 from the annual deductible of $283 in 2026, CMS said.

"The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending," CMS said in a statement.

The Trump administration recently sent $90 checks to 20.8 million middle-class older adults, characterizing the payment as a way to help offset the expected Medicare premium increase.

The Medicare Part B premium is automatically deducted from Social Security checks, eroding part of the recently announced cost-of-living adjustment. The COLA will be 3.6% in 2027, up from 2.8% this year. For the average beneficiary, the COLA will add about $75 to their monthly check.

If your income exceeds specific tiered limits - such as over $112,000 for individual tax returns or $240,00 for married couples for 2027 - you pay an additional monthly surcharge known as the income-related monthly adjustment amount, or IRMAA. This surcharge is added to the standard monthly premiums for Medicare. The 2027 IRMAA surcharges range from $83.70 to $502.40 for an individual depending on income, CMS said.

The news of the new Medicare Part B premium comes during the Medicare open-enrollment period that runs through Dec. 7. Eligible adults can switch from traditional Medicare to a private Medicare Advantage plan, change from one Medicare Advantage plan to another, and join or change a Medicare Part D prescription-drug plan. These changes take effect on Jan. 1.
